relearning.title: Read: the protists
relearning.description: A short reading with the junk-drawer analogy, worked examples and quick checks.

body.text:
**I can give a general description of the organisms in the Kingdom Protista.**

**Think of the junk drawer in your kitchen.** It holds everything that doesn't fit in any other drawer. Kingdom Protista is biology's junk drawer: it holds the **eukaryotes that are not plants, animals or fungi**.

**What all protists share:** every protist is **eukaryotic** (its cells have a nucleus). Most are **unicellular** (one cell), but some, like kelp, are multicellular. Most live in water or damp places.

**Three main types:**
- **Plant-like protists (algae)** have chloroplasts and make their own food by photosynthesis, so they are **autotrophs**. They are grouped by color: green, red, brown (kelp) and golden algae. Tiny floating algae, called **phytoplankton**, feed many ocean animals.
- **Animal-like protists (protozoans)** are **heterotrophs**: they take in food. They are one-celled and most can move. "Protozoa" means "first animals".
- **Fungus-like protists** are the **slime molds** and **water molds**. They feed on dead or decaying material and help recycle it.

**Worked example:** A paramecium is one cell with a nucleus. It has no chloroplasts, eats bacteria and swims with short hairs called cilia. It is an **animal-like protist**.

checks.prompt: Which statement is true of ALL protists?

options.text: They are eukaryotic: their cells have a nucleus
They all make their own food

checks.explanation: Every protist is a eukaryote. Not all are one cell (kelp is multicellular), and only the plant-like ones make their own food.

checks.prompt: A protist has chloroplasts and floats near the ocean surface as phytoplankton. What type is it?
checks.explanation: Chloroplasts mean it makes its own food by photosynthesis, so it is a plant-like protist (an alga).

sections.title: How protozoans move, and why protists matter

body.text:
**Animal-like protists are grouped by how they move:**
- **Sarcodines** move with **pseudopods** ("false feet"), bulges of cytoplasm that stretch out and pull the cell along. Example: the amoeba. It also wraps its pseudopods around food and engulfs it (**phagocytosis**), then digests it in a **food vacuole**.
- **Ciliates** move with **cilia**, short hairs that beat in waves. Example: the paramecium.
- **Flagellates** move with one or more **flagella**, long whip-like tails. Example: the flagellate that causes African sleeping sickness.
- **Sporozoans** can't move on their own. They are parasites that reproduce by spores. Example: *Plasmodium*, which causes **malaria**.

**Worked example 2 (malaria):** An *Anopheles* mosquito bites a person who has malaria and picks up *Plasmodium*. The mosquito bites another person, and *Plasmodium* enters the blood. It hides inside red blood cells, makes spores and bursts the cells. *Plasmodium* needs two hosts: a person and a mosquito.

**Reproduction:** most protozoans reproduce asexually by **binary fission**. A paramecium can also swap genetic material with another paramecium by **conjugation**.

**Why protists matter:** phytoplankton make a large share of Earth's oxygen and are the base of ocean food chains. Protozoans (zooplankton) feed small water animals. Some protists cause diseases: malaria, sleeping sickness and dysentery.

**Watch out for:** calling algae plants (they have no roots, stems or leaves), saying every protist is one cell, calling slime molds fungi, and mixing up cilia (short hairs) with flagella (long tails).

checks.prompt: Malaria is caused by *Plasmodium*. What kind of protist is it?

options.text: A ciliate that swims with cilia
A sporozoan that can't move on its own

checks.explanation: *Plasmodium* is a sporozoan: a parasite with no way to move that spreads by spores and needs a mosquito to reach a new host.

checks.prompt: An amoeba moves by stretching out "false feet". Type their name.
checks.explanation: They are pseudopods (pseudopodia). Cilia are short hairs and flagella are long tails, and the amoeba uses neither.

sections.shortAnswer: Explain how plant-like protists and animal-like protists are different in the way they get food.

relearning.title: Do: flip the protist cards, then classify a mystery protist
relearning.description: Flashcards with a 3-question self-quiz, then a mystery protist classified one step at a time.

cards.back: Eukaryotes that are not plants, animals or fungi. Most are one cell and live in water.
Autotrophs with chloroplasts. Grouped by color: green, red, brown and golden.
One-celled heterotrophs that take in food. Most can move. Grouped by how they move.
Slime molds and water molds. They feed on dead or decaying material.
A "false foot" of cytoplasm an amoeba uses to move and to engulf food.
Short hairs that beat in waves to move a ciliate like the paramecium.
A long, whip-like tail that moves a flagellate.

checks.prompt: Which group of protists makes its own food by photosynthesis?
checks.explanation: Algae have chloroplasts, so they are autotrophs. Protozoans and slime molds both take in food made by other living things.
A paramecium is a ciliate: it is covered in short cilia. The amoeba is the one that uses pseudopods.

checks.prompt: Why are slime molds put in Kingdom Protista instead of Kingdom Fungi?

options.text: They look like fungi but have life cycles unlike true fungi

checks.explanation: Slime molds are fungus-like: they feed on decaying material, but part of their life is spent as moving, amoeba-like cells, which true fungi never do. They have no chloroplasts, and every protist is a eukaryote.

sections.title: Worked problem: classify a mystery protist

body.problem: A single cell from pond water has a nucleus but no chloroplasts. It eats bacteria, and it is covered in short hairs that beat in waves. Classify it.

steps.text: Is it a eukaryote? Yes, it has a nucleus. It is one cell and is not a plant, animal or fungus, so it is a protist.
Does it make its own food? No chloroplasts, and it eats bacteria, so it is a heterotroph. It moves and eats, so it is an animal-like protist (a protozoan).
How does it move? Short hairs that beat in waves are cilia, so it is a ciliate.
The best match is the paramecium: an animal-like protist in the ciliate group.

checks.prompt: Your turn: a protist with chloroplasts floats in a lake and makes its own food. Which type is it?
checks.explanation: Chloroplasts and making its own food mean it is an autotroph: a plant-like protist (an alga). Animal-like protists take in food instead.

checks.prompt: A protist lives inside human red blood cells, can't move on its own and spreads by spores. Which group is it in?
checks.explanation: Sporozoans have no way to move and are parasites that reproduce by spores, like *Plasmodium* (malaria). Sarcodines use pseudopods and flagellates use flagella.
